key_insight: Extending multi-pass weld stops away from the gusset joint and TIG-dressing their notches substantially improved fatigue strength over conventional welded-around details.
engineering_relevance: The technique offers a route to more fatigue-resistant gusset connections, with FAT90 (m = 5) suggested for design under high mean stress based on preliminary analysis.
method: Screened welding and post-weld treatment techniques on S420 steel coupon specimens.
Established characteristic S–N curves using uniaxial constant-amplitude tests at R = 0.1.
Evaluated the selected joint configuration under variable-amplitude block loading in the high-cycle regime.
evidence_signal: Experimental testing yielded a characteristic fatigue strength of 127 MPa at 97.7% survival probability with slope m = 5; variable-amplitude tests further assessed applicability.
watch_item: The FAT90 design recommendation relies on transformation to R = 0.5 and preliminary finite-element estimates of structural stress concentration.
paper_title: Fatigue strength improvement of gusset end detail with welding techniques
